market_holds: Spot 13.615 at the 18:08 UTC seal (Yahoo daily bar showed 14.02 intraday at about 14:30 ET), -17% over 5 sessions, -40% over 20, -71% from the 52-week high and 2% above the 52-week low (sealed baseline). The ADS closed 34.77 after the Q2 print on 2026-08-13, so the stock has lost about 60% since its last report. Options: front (Dec-18) straddle 23.7%, event-implied move 9.4% net of ordinary vol, 25-delta skew +5.25 vol points toward puts, put/call OI 0.7 (baseline). Short interest is roughly 13.7-14.5M ADS, about 6-7 days to cover, up from 11.45M on 2026-09-30 (aggregator pages dated 11-17/11-18, not FINRA primary). Consensus Q3 revenue is about $474M (+17% y/y) and EPS $1.31, which includes non-core items (DayOne dilution gains), per the Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-11-18. That preview predates the 11-16 rule's full sell-off, so the numbers may be stale. Guide: FY26 revenue RMB12.7-13.0bn, adj. EBITDA RMB5.9-6.1bn, capex ~RMB10bn, 1 GW bookings target (470 MW in H1, so about 530 MW implied for H2), net move-ins 235 MW for FY26. The leg down from 11-12 to 11-20 (22.62 to 13.33) lines up with the US BIS interim final rule of 2026-11-16 on remote access to advanced chips in overseas data centres serving China-headquartered firms. That rule hits DayOne directly: GDS holds about 25%, ByteDance was 69% of DayOne's revenue in H1 2026, DayOne capacity is concentrated in Johor and Batam, and its F-1 for a roughly $20bn-valuation US IPO was already being cut back or delayed in October. Earlier legs: 10-14 (-12.8%, global tech sell-off) and 11-12 (-11.4%, chip-sanction fears and a China tech sell-off). There was a 13% bounce on 11-23, then -7% on 11-24.
view: The price is no longer about the China quarter. It has stripped out most of the DayOne option value (the sum-of-parts that carried the equity thesis) and is now pricing leverage risk on a capex-heavy domestic builder. The domestic counterparties point the other way. Tencent's September-quarter capex rose about six-fold, with spending guided at peak levels through 2027 (11-18). Alibaba's capex rose about 60%, with AI cloud revenue +53% (11-19). Cutting Chinese firms off from overseas Nvidia capacity arguably pushes compute demand back onshore, which is GDS's domestic book. So Q3 bookings are likely to keep pace with the 1 GW target, and management will surely argue onshoring on the 07:00 ET call. A further argument may surface: reporting says none of ByteDance's DayOne work is AI training or inference, which could keep DayOne under the 12M TPP threshold. A heavily sold, moderately shorted stock at its lows with a bmo call could therefore bounce hard by 13:00 ET. Against that, Alibaba itself said the rule may cut its long-term 20 GW target and affect its capex plan, and Alibaba is a top GDS customer. Domestic move-ins depend on domestic GPU supply. GDS may be constrained in what it can say about DayOne while DayOne's F-1 is in registration. Any DayOne impairment, IPO shelving, or a softer bookings number or trimmed 1 GW target would extend a move with strong momentum. The last four prints split both ways (Q3'25 US -5% on a beat, Q1'26 HK -13 to -15% on an unchanged guide, Q2'26 +5 to 6% on record bookings), and the stock trades on bookings and guide, not EPS. Net: a slight lean to a relief move, too weak to bet on.
unpriced: Possibly the onshoring argument and the strength of domestic hyperscaler capex (Tencent, Alibaba) relative to a price set by DayOne and leverage fears. But I cannot show that this is outside the price: the rule, the Alibaba and Tencent results and the DayOne exposure are all public and dated within the last 8 days, and the downtrend is persistent. No clear unpriced reaction.

recommendation.reason: The domestic demand evidence (Tencent capex about six-fold, Alibaba capex +60%, record H1 bookings) and the washed-out positioning argue for a relief move. But the decisive unknown is DayOne: its exposure to the 11-16 rule, its IPO and GDS's mark on its 25% stake. I cannot see that ahead of the release, and Alibaba's own warning about capex under the rule cuts the other way. The probability does not reach 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Q3 bookings of 250 MW or more with the 1 GW target reaffirmed, plus management quantifying DayOne's rule exposure as limited (non-AI ByteDance workloads), would make me long. A trimmed bookings target, a DayOne impairment or IPO withdrawal, or a capex raise with weaker funding would make me short.

self_critique: Bull side: a stock 60% below its last print, with consensus anchored to a domestic business whose customers are spending at record rates and a rule that pushes Chinese compute onshore, is a textbook relief-rally setup into a 07:00 ET call, and I may be too timid. Bear side: the trend has been relentless, the 11-24 drop into the print may reflect informed selling, and DayOne could force an impairment or IPO withdrawal disclosed in the release. Both cases are strong, so 56 is near the honest middle.
